issues.description: Email validation regex is too simplistic and may allow invalid emails or miss edge cases
HTML entity encoding is incomplete for XSS prevention and doesn't cover all dangerous characters
Error messages expose internal implementation details that could aid attackers
Email is converted to lowercase but this isn't validated or documented, which could cause issues with case-sensitive email systems
ID generation using Date.now() and Math.random() is not collision-resistant in high-throughput scenarios
Database query is commented out, making this function non-functional in production
Input validation could be more defensive by checking for empty strings and trimming whitespace
No input length validation could allow extremely long inputs that cause performance or storage issues
No error handling for database operation failures - errors will bubble up without context
No duplicate email checking - could create multiple users with same email

codeQuality.summary: The code demonstrates good structure with TypeScript types, input validation, anration is not collision-resistant for production use [MEDIUM], (3) Email validation is too simplistic [MEDIUM], (4) Missing duplicate email checks, length validation, and proper error handling [LOW]. The sanitization approach is basic and should use established libraries. Overall, this is a decent foundation but requires improvements before production use, particularly uncommenting/implementing the database call and using proper UUID generation.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email validation is a security-critical function that determines whether user input is accepted. Incorrect validation could allow malformed emails or reject valid ones. Needs tests for valid emails, invalid formats, edge cases like missing @, missing domain, multiple @, empty string, and special characters.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test suite should include: valid emails (user@example.com, user.name+tag@example.co.uk), invalid emails (no@, @example.com, user@, plain-text, user@domain, multiple@@example.com), edge cases (empty string, whitespace, very long emails, internationalized domains)

untestedPaths.reasoning: Input sanitization is critical for preventing XSS attacks. All possible injection vectors must be tested to ensure security. Missing tests could leave application vulnerable to cross-site scripting attacks.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest:
Test suite should include: basic XSS patterns (), HTML tags (
, ), quotes (single and double), mixed attack vectors (), already-sanitized input (idempotency), empty string, normal text without special characters, and verify exact output matches expected entity encoding

untestedPaths.reasoning: Main business logic function that orchestrates validation, sanitization, and user creation. Must test all validation paths, error conditions, and successful user creation. This is the primary entry point and needs comprehensive coverage.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test suite should include: successful user creation with valid input, missing email error, missing name error, both email and name missing, invalid email format error, email is lowercased correctly, name is sanitized properly, generated user has all required fields (id, email, name, createdAt), saveUser is called with correct parameters, createdAt is a valid Date object

untestedPaths.reasoning: ID generation must produce unique identifiers. While the implementation uses timestamp and random values, tests should verify format consistency and uniqueness to prevent ID collisions.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test suite should include: ID starts with 'user_' prefix, ID contains timestamp component, ID contains random component, multiple calls generate different IDs (uniqueness), ID format matches expected pattern (user_[timestamp]_[random])

untestedPaths.reasoning: Database persistence layer using parameterized queries. While currently stubbed, tests should verify correct query structure and parameter ordering to ensure SQL injection protection when implemented.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test suite should include: verify parameterized query uses correct SQL syntax, verify parameters array contains values in correct order [id, email, name, createdAt], mock database call and verify it's invoked with query and params, test error handling when database operation fails

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email lowercasing is critical to prevent duplicate users with different case variations (User@Example.com vs user@example.com). Must verify case normalization works correctly.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test with emails in various cases: UPPERCASE@EXAMPLE.COM, MixedCase@Example.COM, lowercase@example.com - all should be normalized to lowercase in the final user object

untestedPaths.reasoning: Validation checks should execute in the correct order and provide appropriate error messages. Testing ensures the first validation failure is reported correctly.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test validation order: when both email and name are missing, verify 'Email and name are required' error; when name is present but email is invalid, verify 'Invalid email format' error is thrown

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email regex can have subtle bugs with edge cases like consecutive dots, leading/trailing spaces, or international characters. These edge cases can bypass validation.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test edge cases: emails with spaces (" user@example.com"), consecutive dots (user..name@example.com), dots at start/end (.user@example.com, user.@example.com), missing TLD (user@localhost), IP addresses (user@192.168.1.1), international characters (userñ@example.com)

untestedPaths.reasoning: Sanitization should be idempotent. Double-encoding already sanitized input could cause display issues (e.g., < becoming &lt;).
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test idempotency: pass already-sanitized input like '<script>' and verify it doesn't get double-encoded. Also test mixed content with both raw and encoded entities.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Input validation doesn't trim whitespace. Empty strings or whitespace-only values could pass the truthy check but create invalid users.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test with whitespace inputs: empty strings (''), whitespace-only email ('   '), whitespace-only name ('   '), leading/trailing whitespace in valid input. Verify appropriate validation errors or trimming behavior.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Rapid successive calls within the same millisecond could theoretically generate IDs with the same timestamp. The random component mitigates this, but should be verified.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Generate multiple IDs in rapid succession (e.g., 1000 IDs in a loop) and verify all are unique. Calculate collision probability with the current random string length.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Error path when email is missing must be tested to ensure proper validation and error messaging.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call createUser with { email: '', name: 'Test' } and verify it throws Error with message 'Email and name are required'

untestedPaths.reasoning: Error path when name is missing must be tested to ensure proper validation and error messaging.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call createUser with { email: 'test@example.com', name: '' } and verify it throws Error with message 'Email and name are required'

untestedPaths.reasoning: Error path for invalid email format must be tested to ensure email validation is working correctly.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call createUser with { email: 'invalid-email', name: 'Test' } and verify it throws Error with message 'Invalid email format'

testCoverage.summary: The clean-code.ts file has ZERO test coverage. All 5 exported functions (isValidEmail, sanitizeInput, createUser, generateId, saveUser) and 2 interfaces are completely untested. This is critical because the code handles security-sensitive operations including email validation, XSS prevention through input sanitization, and SQL injection prevention through parameterized queries. There are 14 untested paths identified: 5 functions requiring comprehensive test suites, 6 critical edge cases that could lead to security vulnerabilities or data integrity issues, and 3 error handling branches. Priority breakdown: 8 critical (security and core validation), 5 high (data integrity and uniqueness), 2 medium (user experience and edge cases), 1 low (theoretical collision scenarios). Immediate action required to add test coverage for all security-critical validation and sanitization logic.

suggestions.description: Extract HTML entity escaping into a configurable mapping-based approach for better maintainability and extensibility
suggestions.benefits: Reduces multiple regex passes to a single pass with a character class, improves performance, makes it easier to add/modify entity mappings, and fixes the missing ampersand escaping which should come first in proper HTML sanitization

suggestions.description: Separate validation logic from business logic by extracting validation into a dedicated function
suggestions.benefits: Improves separation of concerns, makes validation logic reusable and testable independently, reduces cognitive load in the main function, and follows the Single Responsibility Principle

suggestions.description: Replace custom ID generation with crypto.randomUUID() for better uniqueness guarantees
suggestions.benefits: Uses cryptographically secure random UUID (RFC 4122 compliant) instead of timestamp + Math.random which can have collisions, eliminates race condition risks when multiple users are created simultaneously, and follows modern Node.js best practices

suggestions.description: Use a more comprehensive email validation regex or library for production use
suggestions.benefits: Handles more email edge cases according to RFC 5322, validates domain structure properly, prevents common validation bypasses, and provides more robust email validation for production use

suggestions.description: Add readonly modifiers to User interface properties to prevent accidental mutations
suggestions.benefits: Prevents accidental mutations of user objects, makes immutability explicit at the type level, helps catch bugs at compile time, and communicates that User is a value object that shouldn't be modified after creation

suggestions.description: Add email sanitization alongside name sanitization for consistency and security
suggestions.benefits: Adds trim() to remove leading/trailing whitespace from both email and name, prevents storage of emails with whitespace which can cause lookup issues, ensures consistent data sanitization across all user inputs, and improves data quality

refactorings.summary: Identified 6 meaningful refactoring opportunities focusing on security improvements (better HTML sanitization with single-pass regex), architectural improvements (validation extraction following SRP), modernization (crypto.randomUUID for better uniqueness), and data integrity (readonly modifiers, input trimming, comprehensive email validation). The most impactful changes are the sanitization optimization, validation separation, and UUID modernization which improve security, maintainability, and reliability.

recommendations.description: Uncomment and implement the database query in saveUser() function. The function currently has a commented-out db.query call on line 86, making it non-functional in production.
Add comprehensive test coverage for all security-critical functions. Currently at 0% coverage with 8 critical untested paths including isValidEmail, sanitizeInput, and createUser validation branches.
Replace simplistic email validation regex with RFC 5322 compliant validation or use a proven library like validator.js to handle edge cases properly.
Replace Date.now() + Math.random() ID generation with crypto.randomUUID() to eliminate collision risks in high-throughput scenarios.
Improve HTML sanitization by using a single-pass regex with character class and add missing ampersand escaping. Consider using established libraries like 'he' or 'DOMPurify' for production.
Extract validation logic into a separate validateCreateUserInput() function to improve separation of concerns and testability.
Add input trimming for both email and name fields to prevent storage of whitespace-padded values that can cause lookup issues.
Add readonly modifiers to User interface properties to prevent accidental mutations and make immutability explicit at the type level.
